html:
The Andoque are a small Indigenous people of the Colombian Amazon, living on the middle Caquetá River near the rapids of Araracuara. They call themselves pʌʌsíʌhʌ. Their language is usually treated as an isolate, related to no other known language.

In the early 1900s the Andoque were caught up in the Putumayo atrocities of the rubber boom, when the Peruvian Amazon Company enslaved the peoples of the region to tap rubber. Their numbers fell to a few hundred. Neighbours on the same rivers include the Murui-Muinane and Bora peoples. Today they live in a reserve in Colombia.
